drugRefs.why: Highly effective tissue amoebicide for invasive disease including liver abscess, with response typically seen within days; first-line for amoebic liver abscess based on strong clinical/imaging suspicion.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Followed by a luminal agent (Paromomycin or Diloxanide furoate)
drugRefs.why: A luminal agent is required after tissue amoebicide therapy to eradicate any colonic cyst carriage, since metronidazole alone does not reliably clear luminal infection and relapse/transmission risk remains otherwise.

drugRefs.coverage: Shorter-course alternative to metronidazole with similar efficacy, also requiring follow-up luminal agent therapy.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Tissue amoebicides provide excellent coverage of the causative organism for invasive disease.
gaps: Luminal cyst carriage is NOT covered by metronidazole/tinidazole alone — a luminal agent is required afterward to prevent relapse/transmission.

stewardship.deescalation: If serology/aspirate confirms isolated amoebic disease and the patient is responding to metronidazole, no antibacterial agents are needed; ensure the luminal agent course is completed after the tissue amoebicide regardless of rapid clinical improvement.

drugs.why: A luminal agent is required after tissue amoebicide therapy to eradicate any colonic cyst carriage, since metronidazole alone does not reliably clear luminal infection and relapse/transmission risk remains otherwise.

framework: Aspiration is generally NOT required for typical amoebic liver abscess that responds to metronidazole — unlike pyogenic abscess, drainage is reserved for large abscesses (>5cm with rupture risk), left-lobe abscesses (pericardial rupture risk), or failure to improve within 5-7 days, where it also helps exclude a pyogenic or mixed process.
Always follow tissue amoebicide therapy with a luminal agent — omitting this step is a common and consequential oversight that risks relapse and continued transmission.

If the clinical/radiological picture is ambiguous between pyogenic and amoebic abscess, empiric metronidazole can reasonably be combined with antibacterial coverage pending aspirate/serology results rather than committing to one diagnosis prematurely.
